piece_title: F4 round 3 — light, sky and atmosphere: the source-side cool day key, measured at four judged windows and shipped OFF

critic.note: I built none of this. My brief handed me the builder's status file first and told me to read `what_i_could_not_do` before anything else — a departure from CRITIC-DOCTRINE §8, recorded in `method_deviations`. It cost less than it usually does: every gap the status file declared, I found on disk exactly as declared. My brief also carried three figures (81 reference items, 141 blind entries, 105 not_possible / 0 run) which I re-derived rather than inherited, and two of the three came out different — see `blind_comparisons`.

blind_comparisons.not_possible_reason: RI-VIS04 declares `blind_pair: no` in its own front matter, so no gate is owed on the item. The judgement F4 exists to move IS blind, and a critic cannot spawn a fresh judge: `create_session` raises an approval prompt and CLAUDE.md rule 0 forbids it; rule 0e places this with the orchestrator and says an unrun gate is a live blocker, not a footnote. Scored 0, fail-closed.
blind_comparisons.census_rederived_by_me_this_turn: MY BRIEF SAID 81 ITEMS / 141 ENTRIES / 105 not_possible / 0 RUN. I re-derived all four and two came out different. Reading front matter rather than grepping — `blind_pair: yes` inside the `---` block, restricted to files carrying `id: RI-*` — **80** reference items declare a blind pair (the `grep -rl` figure is 106; the difference is documents quoting the string). Across 74 verdict JSON files carrying `blind_comparisons` there are **142** entries: **105 not_possible**, **27 done**, 3 not_required, 1 void, 1 not_run, 1 answered-and-revealed. `grep -rEn '"blind_status"[^,]*"run"' corpus/90-verdicts/` returns **0** and every loose-form hit is a document quoting the absence. SO 'ZERO RUN' IS ALSO NOT RIGHT AND I WILL NOT PASS IT ON: the 27 `done` entries carry pack_ids, seeds, blind_pick and reveal — camera series in W1-00, lore in W1-LIBRARY-r1, prose in W1-PROSE-BLIND-r1. I did NOT audit whether any used a fresh judge (S51) and I claim nothing about their validity. The defensible statement is narrower: no VISUAL blind pair has ever run, Protocol A on 2026-08-14 remains the whole visual blind history, and the 80 items are waiting on the orchestrator.

biggest_gap.what: F4'S BAR IS `M6 hue_offset` ON FIVE 512x512 CROPS TAKEN FROM A CHARACTER DECK, AND ON THREE OF THEM THE METRIC'S QUARTILES DO NOT SEPARATE LIT FROM SHADOW. Measured from the round's own same-process `key_off` arms: at pair01 the mask called SHADOW is 65.4% key-lit and the mask called LIT is 26.3% key-lit — inverted, AUC 0.439 — and the picture says the same thing at a glance (LIT_MASK is the sky and a pale wall; SHADOW_MASK is dither speckle on open sunlit ground). At pair02 both quartiles are ~75% key-lit and the split is dark wood against pale stone: albedo, not light. The metric has also never been given a null control and fails one — with the sun at intensity 0 it scores HIGHER at 7 of 8 window/domain pairs, and at pair02's crop it reads 24.70 against a bar of 15. AND THE BUILD ITSELF IS BIMODAL: driven on foot at 13:00 through the plaza it reads hue_offset 18.38 crop / 15.57 frame with retention 0.88/1.11 and C_shadow 6.74/6.29 — the whole exterior_daylight profile passed, on the shipped warm key, nothing changed — while at 08:00, forty metres away, four orbit angles read 8 of 8 below the 6 deg hard fail. Every lever tested in three rounds (the horizon triple, keyWarmth, keyCool, the probe's sun lobe, the ambient's colour and intensity) was screened at pair01, whose mask is inverted.

secondary_observations.what: THE CHANGE IS A BIT-EXACT NO-OP AND THE ROUND HAD THE PROOF WITHOUT NOTICING. `probe/p0-control.png`, `keyhue/k0-control.png` and `before-pair01/pair01__base.png` share sha256 37d7838de3026a24; the three `*-recheck` frames share 588fe71062708002. The first two were served `sky.js 5fd64d93` — the round-2 tree, which has no `keyCool` in it at all — and the third `7172bb96`, the round-3 tree with the branch at 0.00. Two different source trees, three separate browser processes, identical 1920x1080 pixels. I hashed all 62 frames on disk: exactly two duplicate groups exist and both are these intended controls, which also confirms the round's `char-npc` fix is real.

THE SHIPPED TREE HAD NEVER BEEN PHOTOGRAPHED AT A JUDGED WINDOW. Every window run served `7172bb96`; HEAD carries `8cfc715a`. I captured it twice with two tools: pair01 crop 7.35 / 7.38, frame 6.48 / 6.39 / 6.36. Against the round's BEFORE frame the difference is mean |dRGB| 0.0016, max 15, 0.08% of subpixels, with two sibling commits touching NPC motion landed in between. The claim holds; it is now a measurement.

NO POSE DRIFT, AND THIS WAS THE ROUND'S BIGGEST STRUCTURAL RISK. `char-npc` resolves through `listEntities` at capture time in a process separate from its BEFORE twin, so pair03 and pair04 could have been shot from different places. Best integer alignment searched over +/-4 px is (0,0) at all four windows, with mean |dY| 1.119-1.295 and edge IoU 0.8752-0.9353.

A FOURTH INSTRUMENT DEFECT THE BRIEF DID NOT ASK FOR: `SKY_MASK` IS ARM-DEPENDENT. Same pose, same run: pair04's crop reads sky_frac 0.0000 on `base` and 0.2203 on `key_off`; pair02's 0.0000 -> 0.0722. Turning the key off darkens the ground, the P60 threshold moves, and a fifth of the crop reclassifies from foreground to sky — so a base-vs-key_off comparison there compares a 100%-foreground image against a 78%-foreground one. Same family as S60: a measure computed over a domain that moves with the intervention.

AND A FIFTH, MINOR AND IN THE SAFE DIRECTION: `f4r3-capture.mjs:288` steps 3 frames between arms while the deck declares `settle_frames: 12` and `SETTLE` is used at every pose change. Because `base_recheck` is taken four captures after `base`, the published 'noise floor' bundles simulation advance with capture wobble. On this pipeline an identical prefix reproduces BIT-IDENTICAL frames, so there is no stochastic capture noise at all — the 0.11/0.43 deg floors measure how far the world moves in twelve frames, which makes them upper bounds.

THE IDENTITY CONTROL HOLDS, WHICH IS THE THING THAT WOULD HAVE VOIDED THE WHOLE PROBE LEG. `p1-rebake-identity` (the builder's own rebake at the shipped `sunGain 3.0`) reads 7.33 on my instrument against a control of 7.35, inside the run's 0.11 deg floor. The falsification of its own hypothesis stands: deleting the probe's sun lobe entirely is worth +0.38 deg on the crop against a bar of 15, and worse on the frame.

S66'S STATED EVIDENCE IS OVERSTATED AND IT IS THE FIFTH RULING IN THE SAME PATTERN. 'The four windows sort perfectly by cast-shadow area' — ordered ascending (pair02 0.00001, pair01 0.0427, pair04 0.1476, pair03 0.7693) the crop deltas run -0.07, +8.34, -3.17, -11.01. Non-monotone, and it breaks at pair02, the window with the LEAST cast shadow, where S66's mechanism predicts the LARGEST spurious rise and the number does not move at all. The reason is the half S66 omits: the prediction needs BOTH quartiles. ARBITRATION's own tally under S63 and S65 lists S58, S60, S63, S65 as rulings whose rule survived and whose narrated mechanism did not; S66 is the fifth, written the same night the fourth was recorded.

`RI-VIS04` §3-D3'S QUOTED FIGURES DO NOT REPRODUCE, AND THEY ARE IN THE CORPUS. §3-D3 states 'M6 retention fell 0.7199 -> 0.4526 and M6 C_shadow fell 9.762 -> 4.785' at pair03. Measured by me on the round-1 BUILDER's own banked crops (`artifacts/F4-KEY-LIGHT/frames/pair03__{BEFORE-revert,AFTER}__judged-crop.png`, in this repo, no browser needed): 0.3965 -> 0.2321 and 11.176 -> 4.498. arbitration_questions.question: S66 part (a) rules that `M6` carries a precondition — 'a window with cast-shadow area below a floor scores inapplicable'. I drove the camera to two orbit angles at 08:00 and captured `base` + `shadows_off` in the same process. Yaw 270 — a large soft building shadow lying across brightly sunlit stone, the most textbook lit/shadow composition of the four — carries cast-shadow area 0.1025 at tau8, 3.4x §3-D2's floor and 2.4x pair01's, and reads `hue_offset` 0.04 deg. Yaw 000 carries 0.0604 and reads 0.05 deg. A cast-shadow-area floor passes both as valid readings of the illuminant. Meanwhile P(cast-shadowed | SHADOW_MASK) at yaw 270 is only 0.27. IS CAST-SHADOW AREA THE RIGHT PRECONDITION VARIABLE, OR IS IT WHETHER THE QUARTILES LAND ON THE SHADOW?
arbitration_questions.my_ruling_pending_arbitration: It is the quartiles, and §2-D3 clause 1 is the measurable form: `f_key(SHADOW_MASK) <= 0.5 x f_key(LIT_MASK)`, computed from the `key_off` arm S60 already requires. On the four judged crops that clause fails at pair01, pair02 and pair04 and passes only at pair03 — the same three-of-four split S66 reaches, by a variable that also correctly classifies the two orbit angles S66's floor would have let through. S66 parts (b) and (c) are unaffected and I confirm both.

arbitration_questions.question: S64 fixed the domain as the sealed judged crop because 'it is the pixels five blind judges actually looked at'. Those five crops come from a CHARACTER deck (`char-player` and `char-npc` at 2.6 m). On three of the four measured, M6's quartiles do not separate illumination at all (§2-D3 clause 1), and the same shipped build reads 18.38 deg in a driven walk at 13:00 and 0.10 deg at 08:00 forty metres away. MAY A LIGHTING ITEM'S ACCEPTANCE SIT ON A CHARACTER DECK'S WINDOWS, OR MUST F4 GET WINDOWS CHOSEN FOR LIGHTING — with the character crops kept as the blind-pack window and reported, but not as the bar?
arbitration_questions.my_ruling_pending_arbitration: F4 needs its own windows, and the character crops stay as a reported second domain exactly as S64 already does for the full frame. This does not weaken S64 — the blind judgement still sits where the judges looked — it separates 'where the blind pack is drawn' from 'what the acceptance is computed on', which S64 conflated because at the time nobody had shown the two could disagree by 18 degrees.
